title: From Silicon Valley Garages: The Resurgence of Retro Computing
summary: As artificial intelligence dominates the tech landscape, a quiet rebellion is brewing in garages across America: the passionate pursuit of vintage computer collecting. Software engineer Josh Dersch embodies this growing movement, painstakingly restoring classic machines and preserving a tangible piece of computing history.
content:
In an era obsessed with AI's next frontier, some tech enthusiasts are looking backward, not forward. Josh Dersch, a software engineer nestled in the heart of Mountain View, California, isn't chasing silicon's bleeding edge; he's meticulously resurrecting its past, one dusty motherboard at a time.

Dersch is far from alone in his vintage obsession. A burgeoning community of collectors is dedicating countless hours to saving machines once destined for the digital dustbin. For many, the thrill lies in a potent mix of nostalgia – a chance to relive the early days of computing – and a deep appreciation for the foundational hardware that paved the way for today's digital world. It’s about more than just owning a piece of history; it’s about understanding its mechanics.

His garage serves as a digital archaeology lab, where Dersch tirelessly coaxes life back into decades-old machines, from classic Apple IIs to early IBM PCs. It’s a labor of love demanding patience, technical know-how, and a keen eye for arcane components, transforming forgotten relics into functioning pieces of history. The satisfaction comes not just from a successful boot-up, but from reconnecting with technology on a fundamental level.

As algorithms grow more abstract and devices increasingly disappear into the cloud, these tangible artifacts offer a comforting counter-narrative. They represent an era when computing felt more accessible, more understandable, and infinitely more tactile. This isn't just about collecting; it's about preserving a mechanical memory, ensuring that the roots of our digital age aren't lost in the relentless march of progress.
keyTakeaways: A growing community of enthusiasts, like software engineer Josh Dersch, are passionately collecting and restoring vintage computers.
The appeal stems from a blend of nostalgia, the technical challenge of restoration, and a desire to preserve early computing history.
This trend offers a tangible counterpoint to the abstract nature of modern AI and cloud computing, emphasizing a hands-on connection to technology.
author: Associated Press
